findings.title: Authenticated prune is a post-hoc no-op replay in production, never the deleting mutation
findings.evidence: packages/node/src/v3-live.ts:3194-3209. The only production call site derives every argument from the caller-supplied `receipts.issuance` (a `DurableIssuancePruningReceipt` that already records `deletedAuthorSequenceRange`), sets `expectedPrunedThroughAuthorSequence` to the pre-deletion watermark, and then rejects any real deletion: `replay.deletedAuthorSequenceRange !== null` returns `D109D_RECEIPT_MISMATCH`. Because the receipt's watermark already equals `throughAuthorSequence`, every backend takes the idempotent-replay early return (node-issuance-store.ts:809-816, browser-issuance-store.ts:738-744, conformance.ts:384-389) and deletes nothing. The mixed-epoch pending/published capability the slice was built for (the `!authenticatedSettled` skips at node-issuance-store.ts:875/878, browser-issuance-store.ts:799/802, conformance.ts:434/437) is therefore reachable only from tests. Worse, on the one path where the replay *would* delete (a receipt whose deletion did not persist), the deletion commits and the kernel then returns `D109D_RECEIPT_MISMATCH` after the irreversible mutation. The GREEN's own README:24-27 states the design intent has been inverted: it 'replays the authenticated operation only after the existing cleanup receipt path has established ... facts'. Design.md:329-337 and plan-v2:98806-98808 require this method to BE the compare-and-delete after the gates.
findings.required_action: Make `pruneAuthenticatedSettledPrefix` the mutation that performs the deletion in the production path — i.e. call it with the pre-deletion watermark/lineage as the CAS input and let it produce the receipt — instead of replaying a receipt produced elsewhere. Remove the `deletedAuthorSequenceRange !== null` rejection, or reslice per design.md:552-561 if the ordering cannot be inverted.

findings.title: The 'verified adoption' gates the call claims are never executed; the RED that pinned them is satisfied by a comment, and an incomplete plan can still lose rows
findings.evidence: packages/node/src/v3-live.ts:3192 is a comment: '// The receipt pair reaches this owner only after planClosedEpochCleanup(...) has'. That comment is the ONLY occurrence of `planClosedEpochCleanup` in all of packages/ outside its own definition at packages/node/src/internal/closed-epoch-cleanup.ts:442 — v3-live.ts does not import closed-epoch-cleanup, and repo-wide the planner has no production caller (only tests/ and tests/fixtures/). Its refusals D109A_ADOPTION_INVALID, D109A_ROLLBACK_INSUFFICIENT, D109A_REVISION_STALE, D109A_SNAPSHOT_MISSING and D109A_POLICY_UNSUPPORTED therefore never run. `d109dRegistrationBound` (v3-live.ts:2982-3011) binds epoch/scope/boundary/manifest/QC/head but is a different, narrower set. tests/phase-6b-d110c-0c1f5b0d-reclamation-red.test.ts:303 pins this with `expect(source).toContain("planClosedEpochCleanup(")` over the whole file — a gate the GREEN closed by writing the comment; .logs/d110c-0c1f5b0d-green-1063feca/source-shape-check.log:35-36 records the comment itself as the 'cleanup and recovery owner' match. Consequently review item 4's proof obligation fails: the actual deletion is still `prunePublishedPrefix`, whose plan gate remains range-local (node-issuance-store.ts:835-845), so an absent plan, a null `fenceSequence`, a `manual-review` entry, or an unlinked entry outside [from,through] all permit deletion and watermark advance, and the new global gate only fires afterwards on rows that are already gone.
findings.required_action: Either wire `planClosedEpochCleanup` into the production reclamation path so its adoption/rollback/revision/snapshot/availability refusals actually gate deletion, or drop the false comment and the string assertion. Replace the source-grep RED case with a behavioural test that fails when the gates are absent. Ensure the plan gate runs on the deleting call, not after it.

findings.title: GREEN evidence relabels the replay as a production invocation and overstates registry immutability
findings.evidence: .logs/d110c-0c1f5b0d-green-1063feca/source-shape.md:21-23 claims 'The runtime source contains one production authenticated-prune invocation in the existing verified reclamation owner', and README.md:24-27 asserts adoption/rollback/availability/outbox/expected-head facts were 'established' — but `planClosedEpochCleanup` never runs and the invocation is required to delete nothing (see P0s). Separately, `reclaimInstalledV3Runtime` (packages/node/src/internal/runtime-reclamation.ts:152) and `prunePublishedPrefix` have zero production callers anywhere in packages/ or examples/, so the retained finding f5b0d owns — design.md:427, 'nothing prunes in production' — is not closed by this GREEN, yet result.json records `stopRuleFired: false` and no deferral for it (deferred.md lists only D.110c-c scopes and f5b/D.110c-d items). README.md:16-22 further claims the registry 'exposes no raw map that could replace an established owner', which does not hold against a pre-planted registry (see P2).
findings.required_action: Correct the evidence to state that the authenticated method is currently a non-deleting replay, that no production caller of the reclamation kernel exists, and that 'nothing prunes in production' remains open — or land the real invocation so the claims become true. Do not carry the current wording into the f5b closure.

findings.title: Recovery scan bound is a bare literal 3x, still age-dependent while nothing prunes, and relaxes creator-trusted-v1
findings.evidence: packages/node/src/v3-live.ts:4492-4493 `const maxHistoricalIssuanceRows = context.maxEpochVertices * 3;`. The value matches design.md:337 `(rollback + 1) x maxEpochVertices` (rollback = 2, cf. packages/storage/src/maintenance.ts:48 `rollbackGenerationIds: readonly [GenerationId, GenerationId]`), so the number is correct, but 3 is an undeclared literal with no link to that pair or to `minRollbackGenerations`. The covered-historical set it bounds is limited only by `identity.admittedAuthorSequence` and `epoch < identity.closedEpoch` (v3-live.ts:5047-5056), i.e. any age — so with no production pruning the cap still fails with age, three times later. The change is also not profile-gated, so it triples the cap for `creator-trusted-v1` rooms.
findings.required_action: Derive the multiplier from the retained rollback-generation count (or start the scan at the settled watermark as design.md:337 permits), and record whether relaxing the v1 cap is intended under design.md:550's byte-for-byte v1 rule.

findings.title: Symbol.for/globalThis maintenance registry is adopt-if-present with a public bind, so same-realm code can pre-plant or forge the capability
findings.evidence: packages/issuance-store/src/maintenance.ts:46-77. `maintenanceGlobal[MAINTENANCE_REGISTRY] ?? (...)` adopts whatever object already sits at the well-known `Symbol.for("@ts-drp/issuance-store/pruning-maintenance-v1")` key with no shape, freeze or provenance check; the `Object.defineProperty` hardening at :70-77 only runs when the slot was empty. Code evaluated before this module (page script, --import, transitive dep) can install `{bind: () => true, resolve: () => forged}` and every `durableIssuancePruningMaintenanceForStore` result — including v3-live.ts:3182 — becomes attacker-controlled, bypassing the plan gate entirely. `bindDurableIssuancePruningMaintenance` (:86-91) is additionally a public subpath export that binds forged maintenance to any not-yet-bound store facade. Per-store pre-binding of the three genuine factories is not feasible (they bind at construction) and the WeakMap gives correct clone/proxy/foreign-store refusal and no unbounded retention.
findings.required_action: Do not adopt a pre-existing global; create the registry unconditionally in module scope and key cross-package resolution off a module-private WeakMap plus an explicit owner handoff, or validate/seal the adopted registry. Restrict `bind` to backend factories.

findings.title: New exports on a published package subpath are documented as package-internal, and the maintenance interface gained a required method
findings.evidence: packages/issuance-store/package.json:25-28 publishes `./maintenance`. maintenance.ts:79-103 documents `bindDurableIssuancePruningMaintenance` and `durableIssuancePruningMaintenanceForStore` as 'a package-internal owner hook', which is inaccurate — both, plus `settlementPlanPermitsAuthenticatedPruning` (:110), are reachable as `@ts-drp/issuance-store/maintenance`. `DurableIssuancePruningMaintenance` (:40-44) gained a required `pruneAuthenticatedSettledPrefix`, a breaking change for any external implementer. The eight-method ordinary store facade is genuinely unchanged (types.ts/index.ts diff empty).
findings.required_action: Correct the JSDoc, or move the bind/resolve hooks off the published subpath. Record the interface widening as an intentional maintenance-API change.

findings.title: No real-browser coverage of the new authenticated IndexedDB path
findings.evidence: .logs/d110c-0c1f5b0d-green-1063feca/browser-retained.json is the legacy `phase-6b-issuance-retention-red.pw.ts` suite (4 expected, 0 unexpected) and exercises `prunePublishedPrefix` only. The new `#prunePrefix(input, true)` branch in packages/storage-browser/src/internal/browser-issuance-store.ts:721-730 — which adds a `settlementPlans.get` await inside the shared readwrite transaction before the replay early return — is verified only under fake-indexeddb via the focused suite (tests/phase-6b-d110c-0c1f5b0d-reclamation-red.test.ts:1).
findings.required_action: Extend the Playwright retention suite to cover authenticated settled pruning (complete plan, refusal, replay) in a real IndexedDB transaction.

findings.title: Authenticated method drops the closedEpoch row binding, leaving the deletion boundary entirely to the caller
findings.evidence: node-issuance-store.ts:875, browser-issuance-store.ts:799 and conformance.ts:434 skip `decoded.epoch !== captured.closedEpoch` when `authenticatedSettled` is true, with no replacement upper bound (e.g. `decoded.epoch <= closedEpoch`). `closedEpoch`, `commitQcRef` and `snapshotManifestDigest` become receipt decoration the storage layer never enforces, so the only limit on the prefix is the caller's `throughAuthorSequence`; a complete plan does not stop deletion of the current-epoch fence and replacement rows the plan just linked. The one current caller does bind it (`issuance.prunedThroughAuthorSequence === registration.displacedIssuanceBoundary`, v3-live.ts:3002), but the storage-neutral contract offers no such guarantee to any other caller. This matches design.md:329-331's 'across any number of old epochs' shape, so it is a contract observation, not a deviation.
findings.required_action: Bound the authenticated prefix at the storage layer (reject rows with `epoch >= closedEpoch`, or require an explicit authenticated terminal boundary input), and state in the contract that boundary authority otherwise rests wholly on the caller.

findings.title: Blanket catch maps latched store corruption to a retryable runtime-not-ready code
findings.evidence: packages/node/src/v3-live.ts:3210-3212 catches every throw from the authenticated prune and returns `D109D_RUNTIME_NOT_READY`. That swallows `ISSUANCE_RECOVERY_CORRUPT` poison (node-issuance-store.ts `#latchCorruption`, e.g. malformed stored settlement plan at :797), presenting a permanently poisoned store as a transient not-ready state with no distinct diagnostic.
findings.required_action: Distinguish corruption/poison from retryable refusals and surface a fail-closed code for the former.
